rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with vitamin K (vitamin K, phylloquinone, phytonadione, menaquinone, menatetrenone, vitamin K2, vitamin K1) in its title or abstract, in papers about supplements, fortified food, intake or diet; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving vitamin K, with vitamin K in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Historical screening decisions and review choices are retained. Exact screening inputs and per-decision model provenance were not recorded, so they are not validated for current inputs. Legacy file attribution is shown per outcome; these decisions need fresh screening before a new build may select them.
Overlap is not shown: a bibliography can cite background or excluded trials and cannot establish which studies a review included or pooled.
